title: P02 follow-up: raise decoupled weight decay on the Muon matrices from 10x to 30x (MUON_WD 0.1 -> 0.3) on the 070 incumbent, logging handoff spectral norms
description: P02 follow-up (Muon weight decay, continuing 069/070-claude's 1x->3x->10x keeps at 316/327/353): the only training edit raises the Muon group's decoupled weight decay from 10x to 30x the AdamW per-step shrinkage (MUON_WD 0.1 -> 0.3; peak per-step shrinkage 1e-3 -> 3e-3), leaving the AdamW group, LRs, batch, schedule and init identical to incumbent 070-claude, and adds a stats-only log of every 2-D weight's spectral norm at handoff. 070 improved RL from round 1 onward on every seed, consistent with smaller Muon weights being easier for the frozen RL AdamW to move; this locates where that trend breaks, and the norms give the first direct check of the weight-size mechanism.
hypothesis: Decoupled decay sets Muon weight norms by an update/decay equilibrium (aligned directions saturate at spectral scale ~1/wd, noise directions at ~sqrt(lr/(2 wd))). The frozen RL AdamW (lr 3e-4) takes roughly fixed per-element steps, so its relative step is ~lr_RL/||W||: smaller pretrained weights make expert iteration move the policy further per round, which 069/070 matched (RL-solved and round-4 sample accuracy up on every seed with val loss flat). At 30x the aligned-direction ceiling drops from ~10 to ~3.3 (x shape scale). That is still ~10x the orthogonal init's 0.32 and LayerNorm gains (AdamW, not in the Muon group) can restore attention and readout sharpness, so if the mechanism is plasticity the gain should continue. Counter-mechanism: the angular effective LR of decayed weights grows like sqrt(2 lr wd) (x1.7 here), so the handed-off weights carry more late-step noise, much like the Muon LR increase that hurt in 055; if that dominates, val loss rises and RL starts from a weaker policy.
expected_delta: -80 to +30 theorems at >=7 (central guess -10; bar is 070's exact mean 352.67). Pretraining: steps ~4750-4790 unchanged; final val loss within +0.01 of 070's 0.0911/0.0913/0.0961 (a larger rise = the noise/sharpness failure). If plasticity continues: RL-solved above 070's 788/783/838 on at least two seeds. Norms (no baseline; first measurement): every Muon matrix below its equilibrium ceiling (~1.13 x shape scale / 0.3, i.e. <3.8 for proj/fc2/head, <7.5 for fc1, <6.6 for stacked qkv), emb.weight unaffected by the change. Risk: 070 already used up to 1079 s of the 1200 s total, so longer RL samples could time out a seed.

arch.change: none versus 070-claude: 5 untied fork GPT blocks, d_model 256, 8 heads (head dim 32), d_ff 1024, RoPE base 10000, LayerNorm, GELU, untied embedding/readout
arch.checkpoint_reconstruction: GPT(vocab, 5, 256, 8) from the fork; model.cfg records n_layer=5 and the state dict has blocks.0-blocks.4
arch.kv_cache: one fork KV-cache dict per logical block (5 per sample), unchanged fork code

optimizer.name: split-QKV Muon on hidden matrices and the output readout head.weight throughout; continuous AdamW auxiliary (unchanged from 070-claude except Muon weight decay)

muon.precision: bf16 Newton-Schulz; fp32 momentum and parameters
muon.shape_scale: sqrt(max(1, rows/columns)) per orthogonalized matrix: Q/K/V each 1, attention output 1, fc1 2, fc2 1, head (99,256) 1
muon.schedule: same warmup/cosine fraction as AdamW; muon_lr = 0.01 * adam_lr / 0.001
muon.parameters: All 20 hidden projection parameters (4 per block x 5 blocks) plus head.weight (99,256; vocab 99, no bias) are in Muon: 21 matrices. Five qkv.weight matrices of shape (768,256) use independent Q/K/V updates, represented as a batch of three (256,256) matrices; proj/fc1/fc2 and head are orthogonalized whole. head is wide (99<256) so it is not transposed and its update has 99 singular values near 1.
muon.license: MIT; full copyright and permission notice retained in pretrain.py
muon.qkv_split: After elementwise Nesterov momentum, reshape each QKV update to (3,256,256); independently Frobenius-normalize and run five batched Newton-Schulz steps; reshape back before applying. No extra learning-rate multiplier. Momentum and weight decay stay elementwise and unchanged.

optimizer.adamw_parameters: emb.weight, all projection biases and LayerNorm parameters (incl. ln_f) throughout; head.weight and hidden matrices never enter pretraining AdamW
optimizer.decay_convention: CHANGED: MUON_WD = 30 * WD * LR / MUON_LR = 0.3 (070-claude: 10x = 0.1), so Muon lr*0.3 is thirty times the auxiliary AdamW lr*0.1 per-step shrinkage at every schedule fraction (peak 3e-3 per step instead of 1e-3; decay time constant ~333 steps at peak LR and ~3.3k at the 0.1 LR floor, instead of ~1000/~10k). Applies to all 21 Muon matrices including head.weight. AdamW group decay (wd 0.1 at lr 1e-3) is unchanged. Summed over ~4770 steps (mean schedule factor ~0.55) the cumulative multiplicative decay factor is ~exp(-7.9)=4e-4 instead of ~exp(-2.6)=0.07, so the orthogonal init is fully forgotten and handoff weights are set by the decay/update equilibrium: a consistently aligned direction saturates at spectral scale ~1/0.3 = 3.3 x shape scale (was ~10).
optimizer.clipping: joint global gradient norm 1.0 before both optimizers
optimizer.handoff: standard GPT weights only; pretraining optimizer states are discarded and frozen RL creates its own unchanged AdamW

config.init: Exactly 070-claude (and 069-claude): fork default construction with 5 blocks, then orthogonal_ on every 2D block parameter (gain 0.02*sqrt(max(rows, cols))); embedding and readout keep the fork normal(0.02); biases zero. Initial weights and data order/shift RNG streams per seed identical to 070-claude.
config.diagnostics: NEW, no effect on training or the handed-off model: after the pretraining loop, stats['spectral_norms'] records the fp32 CPU spectral norm (torch.linalg.matrix_norm ord=2, 4 d.p.) of every 2-D parameter at handoff: 20 block matrices (qkv whole, proj, fc1, fc2 per block), head.weight and emb.weight (AdamW, as a comparison). 22 small SVDs, well under 1 s, inside the 15 s grace.
